sourceCoverage.note: Government planning direction; no issuer disclosure is needed for this policy record.
No exchange or market regulator filing is part of this Scottish planning direction.
No earnings release or call is relevant to this policy record.
The Direction defines power capacity as total proposed electrical power and sets the planning EIA threshold; it does not grant site, grid or construction approval.
Read the published Direction and Chief Planner letter: qualifying new data-centre projects over 50MW are EIA development from 17 September 2026.
This is a statutory planning direction, not a technical standard.
No project developer, customer or supplier statement is needed to establish the Direction.
The official Scottish Government publication is the public primary record; no media claim is used.

change.description: The Scottish Government published a new Direction that takes effect on 17 September 2026 and makes qualifying new data-centre developments above 50MW EIA development.

impact.affected: New Scottish data-centre proposals with more than 50MW of total proposed electrical power.
impact.consequence: Environmental assessment becomes an explicit planning-path requirement, affecting siting, design and approval timing without creating a moratorium or project approval.

sources.finding: The Direction takes effect on 17 September 2026; it covers new data-centre developments with total proposed electrical power exceeding 50MW and specifies that qualifying development is EIA development.

primaryAttempts.note: Official publication and Direction read directly; the record supports the threshold, commencement date and planning scope used in public copy.
